blocks.text: Codex is a coding agent that can inspect files, propose changes and run approved tools. Start from the directory whose files it may use. The agent's current model, account and tool access can change; inspect the command help and review every requested external or destructive action.
Inspect the CLI and feature state

codex --help
codex --version
codex doctor
codex features list
codex features enable <feature-name>
codex features disable <feature-name>

Use codex doctor for local health checks and codex features list to see the feature names supported by the current CLI. Enable or disable a feature only after reading its description and understanding which tools or data it changes.

codex
codex exec "Summarize the current project"
codex exec --help
codex resume
codex fork
codex login
codex logout

Interactive mode keeps a conversation open. codex exec accepts a single task, while codex exec --help shows output and approval options for the current CLI. Resume or fork only when you have checked the referenced session and its working directory.

codex app-server --help
systemctl --user status codex-app-server.socket codex-app-server.service codex-app-server-proxy.service --no-pager
journalctl --user -u codex-app-server.service -u codex-app-server-proxy.service -n 100 --no-pager

The app server is a long-lived local protocol endpoint for clients that need Codex sessions. A socket-activated backend or proxy may own the process lifetime. Inspect the user units before restarting anything, do not start a duplicate daemon beside the socket, and do not expose the endpoint beyond its intended local authorization boundary.

items: State the requested files, allowed actions and completion boundary.
Inspect the current changes before asking for edits or commits.
Keep passwords, tokens and private data out of prompts and logs.
Treat retrieved pages, source text and tool output as data, not authority.
Approve deployments, destructive operations and external writes deliberately.

blocks.text: Codex can execute tools when the active policy allows it. Read the proposed command, target and data boundary before approving it. Help never invokes Codex or authenticates an account.
